subject: general
question: A shopkeeper buys pencils from a wholesaler at Rs. 20 for 40 pencils. He sells those pencils at Rs. 20 for 20 pencils. What was his profit or loss percent?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Equalize the quantity of pencils to compare **Cost Price (CP)** and **Selling Price (SP)**.

**CP** of 40 pencils = ₹20

**SP** of 20 pencils = ₹20 ⇒ **SP** of 40 pencils = ₹20 × 2 = ₹40

Since **SP** is double the **CP**, the **Profit** is 100%.

**∴ The correct answer is 100% Profit.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total pencils bought = 40

**Cost Price (CP)** of 40 pencils = ₹20

**Selling Price (SP)** of 20 pencils = ₹20

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ffc2c25c3652b45165b385e180dbe8b293fdef83fa7c128efb5d96d61f3ef990.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Profit = **Selling Price (SP)** − **Cost Price (CP)**

Profit % = (Profit / **Cost Price**) × 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ **CP** of 1 pencil = 20 / 40 = ₹0.50

⇒ **SP** of 1 pencil = 20 / 20 = ₹1.00

⇒ Profit per pencil = ₹1.00 − ₹0.50 = ₹0.50

⇒ Profit % = (0.50 / 0.50) × 100

⇒ Profit % = 1 × 100 = 100%

**∴ The correct answer is 100% Profit.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit/Loss on Quantity

When the investment is the same, Profit % = [(CP Quantity − SP Quantity) / SP Quantity] × 100.

Selling Price Calculation

SP = CP × (100 + Profit%) / 100 or SP = CP × (100 − Loss%) / 100.

Markup Percentage

Markup % = [(Marked Price − Cost Price) / Cost Price] × 100.
